causes.text: Global mergers and acquisitions (M&A) activity fell 36% year-on-year in Q2 2023 as high interest rates and a standoff over the U.S. debt ceiling made companies hesitant to do deals. Dealmakers said the uncertain macro environment and elevated borrowing costs kept executives on the sidelines, leading to sharply lower deal volume and value across the United States and other regions.

source_info.title: Global mergers and acquisitions plunge in second quarter, dealmakers see green shoots

effects.text: On Oct. 18 2023, Morgan Stanley reported that its third-quarter profit fell about 9% to $2.4 billion as sluggish dealmaking and weak trading weighed on results. The bank's investment-banking revenue dropped 27% from a year earlier and net new assets in its wealth-management unit slowed; investors were disappointed and the shares fell 6.5% intraday.

source_info.title: Morgan Stanley profit shrinks as deal slump lingers

causal_reasoning_chain.description: During the second quarter of 2023, high interest rates and the U.S. debt-ceiling standoff curtailed corporate confidence. Dealmakers noted that executives preferred to postpone transactions rather than pay more for financing or risk public backlash, causing global M&A volumes to tumble by over a third compared with the prior year.

The sharp decline in deal flow eroded the pipeline of advisory work for investment banks like Morgan Stanley. With fewer deals to advise on, and clients parking cash in money-market funds instead of investing, Morgan Stanley's investment banking and wealth management revenues weakened considerably.

When Morgan Stanley reported earnings on Oct. 18 2023, the impact of the M&A slump became visible: profit dropped 9%, investment-banking revenue fell 27%, and wealth-management inflows slowed. Investor disappointment led to a 6.5% decline in the share price on the day of the announcement.

rationale: The plunge in global M&A due to high borrowing costs and fiscal uncertainty directly reduced Morgan Stanley's deal pipeline and advisory revenue. With fewer transactions to underwrite, the bank's profits fell and investors responded by selling the stock, creating a clear causal link between the macro M&A slowdown and Morgan Stanley's earnings slump.
counterfactual_analysis: If interest rates had remained low and the debt-ceiling standoff had been resolved quickly, corporate boards may have proceeded with more transactions. In such a scenario, Morgan Stanley's investment-banking revenue would likely have held up, and its shares might not have fallen so sharply.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Heightened geopolitical risk and stock-market swings could independently depress trading revenue and investor sentiment, contributing to profit weakness beyond M&A activity.

details.commentary: When overall deal volumes shrink, competition among investment banks for a smaller pool of mandates becomes more intense. Morgan Stanley must accept lower fees or more aggressive terms to win business, eroding its bargaining power relative to clients in a weak M&A environment.

Higher interest rates, volatile markets and regulatory uncertainty pushed many companies to delay or cancel transactions. Those macro headwinds directly suppressed M&A activity, which flowed through to Morgan Stanley's advisory revenues and drove the negative earnings surprise.

As deal pipelines thin out, fee income drops, leading management to cut costs and rein in risk taking. That retrenchment can further slow origination and prolong the slump in activity, keeping investor expectations for Morgan Stanley's earnings subdued.
